newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank union urges no overtime before Telekom.
newsitem.headline: German bank union urges no overtime before Telekom.

text.p: German white-collar workers union DAG said on Friday that it was instructing its members in the banking sector not to agree to overtime work in protest at sick pay cuts being made by Germany's top three banks.

A union spokesman said it believed overtime work by bank employees would be needed in the coming weeks before the November 18 bourse introduction of Deutsche Telekom AG, Europe's largest-ever flotation.
"We are working on the assumption that the Telekom issue is not possible without overtime in the sector," DAG spokesman Ingo Schwope said in response to enquiries.
Schwope said the union planned other protest action next week about which he could give no details.

The Deutsche Telekom issue has attracted an unprecedented amount of public interest in Germany. Some three million small investors are estimated to have applied for shares, a demand which will require huge administrative resources to process.

Schwope said it was not yet urging bank employees to launch warning strikes against the proposed 20 percent cut to sick pay entitlements, although wage contracts in the banking sector meant such action was immediately open to them.
Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank and Commerzbank are all implementing a controversial new federal law cutting sick pay from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent.

Huge protests against the cuts have already been organised in the metal and engineering industry by the IG Metall trade union, which argues that such cuts would breach clauses protecting full sick pay in existing metal sector wage deals.

DAG on the other hand acknowledges that wage contracts in the banking sector do not specifically guarantee sick payments at 100 percent of salary but wants to negotiate a compromise with the employers.
